summary: Frontend testing of 8 fixes + regression. Found a CRITICAL compilation blocker (ImageEditModal.jsx referenced an undefined ESLint rule 'jsx-a11y/img-redundant-alt' in a disable-next-line comment, which made the whole frontend fail to compile and show the 'Compiled with problems' overlay covering the login page). I fixed it by removing the orphan eslint-disable comment and renaming the alt text to 'preview'. After the fix, app boots and login succeeds. Verified FIX 1 (z-index 9000), FIX 2 (--bp-primary swaps to #9D4E5A for rose and #5A8FE5 for cobalt), FIX 4 (sidebar has distinct 'Projects' and 'Sito Web' sections, Projects Studio is under Sito Web), FIX 5 (user menu computed bg = rgb(15,15,16), opacity=1, backdrop-filter=none — fully opaque). FIX 2 button propagation visually confirmed via screenshot under cobalt (Nuovo Editorial Master button renders with cobalt-blue tint, not teal). FIX 3 / 6 / 7 / 8 were NOT fully verified via DOM probing due to test-script time/selector limitations on the picker modal opening flow, but the static code review confirms the required data-testids and DOM strings exist exactly as specified.

The 'Compiled with problems' overlay covered the entire UI and made the SPA unusable. rca of the issue: The 'Compiled with problems' overlay blocker (visible on /auth/login as 'Definition for rule jsx-a11y/img-redundant-alt was not found') was caused by an inline ESLint disable comment referencing a rule that is not registered in the project's ESLint config (jsx-a11y plugin not wired in). When CRA's react-scripts ESLint webpack loader encounters an inline disable for an unknown rule, it raises this as a compile error (not just a warning), aborting the bundle and triggering the runtime error overlay. Fix: remove the disable-next-line comment and change the alt text to a generic 'preview' string that won't trigger jsx-a11y/img-redundant-alt anyway (the rule flags alt text containing 'image', 'photo', 'picture'). Alternative fix the main agent may prefer: add 'jsx-a11y' plugin to eslintConfig in package.json so the rule is recognized.
